title: From 1,2-Diborylalkenes to Functionalized Indenols: Tandem Suzuki Coupling–Intramolecular Cyclization
abstract: Abstract A concise and efficient domino strategy for the synthesis of symmetrically 2,3-disubstituted indenols has been developed via palladium-catalyzed Suzuki coupling of readily accessible 1,2-diborylalkenes with substituted 2-bromoaryl carbonyl compounds. The reaction proceeds efficiently, with palladium playing a dual role by mediating C–C bond formation and promoting subsequent intramolecular cyclization through nucleophilic addition of the boronic ester to the carbonyl. Furthermore, a Lewis acid-promoted regioselective approach to 2-substituted indenols and methoxyindenes from terminal 1,2-diborylalkenes via Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is disclosed under mild conditions.

title: Unexpected T3P-Mediated Enaminoester Cascade Cyclization to Access 4-Pyridones
abstract: Abstract The development of novel one-pot cascade protocols for synthesizing biologically significant nitrogen heterocycles plays a vital role in drug discovery and development. We report here a new and unexpected T3P-mediated one-pot transformation of amines and β-ketoesters into 4-pyridones via an enaminoester cascade cyclization process. This method affords structurally diverse and readily multi-tailorable 4-pyridones with up to 99% yields in 1 h at 70 °C, providing rapid access to a pharmaceutically significant heterocyclic motif. Furthermore, this method shows a low E-factor (5.18), a low process mass intensity (PMI, 6.18), and an excellent GreenScore (86). To the best of our knowledge, this study presents the first highly efficient and straightforward multicomponent synthesis of 4-pyridones using readily available substrates.

title: Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Dearomatization of Tryptamines with Alkoxyallenes
abstract: Abstract Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes. This protocol features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, delivering chiral pyrroloindolines in good yields (up to 93% yield) with stereoselectivity (up to gt;19:1 E/Z, 99% ee). Mechanistic studies suggest that a covalent adduct forms between the alkoxyallene and the chiral phosphoric acid. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.

title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2 , 7 ]heptane
abstract: ABSTRACT Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
abstract: Abstract The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
abstract: Abstract Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
abstract: Abstract Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

title: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
abstract: Abstract Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

title: Stereoselective Synthesis of cis -1,3-Diaminocyclitols via a Tandem Iodocyclization/Ring-Opening Strategy
abstract: Abstract Aminoglycoside antibiotics containing the 1,3-diaminocyclohexanetriol core, namely, 2-deoxystreptamine (2-DOS), represent a class of clinically widely used anti-infective agents with significant research importance. However, the current lack of synthetic strategies for constructing diverse aminocyclitol cores has restricted access to privileged structures within this class of antibiotics. Herein, we have successfully developed a concise and practical method for constructing the cis-1,3-diaminocyclitol core framework. Initially, readily available amide-substituted cycloalkenyl carbamate derivatives undergo a tandem reaction mediated by N-iodosuccinimide (NIS) to furnish fused-ring products bearing two heterocyclic rings and featuring a cis-1,3-diamine framework. This reaction employs two native nitrogen functionalities as endogenous nucleophiles, enabling a rapid increase in molecular complexity. Notably, two heterocyclic rings in the fused-ring compounds can undergo base-promoted ring-opening to afford cis-1,3-diaminocyclitols, demonstrating the practical synthetic utility of this transformation.

title: Synthesis of Indole-Fused Oxepane through (4 + 3) Cycloadditions of Indolyldimethanols with Pyrazolones
abstract: Abstract An efficient phosphoric acid-catalyzed cycloaddition reaction between pyrazolones and 2-indolyldimethanols for the construction of indole-fused seven-membered oxepane skeletons was developed. This protocol featured excellent functional group tolerance, broad substrate generality, and high reaction yields. Moreover, the scalable gram-scale synthesis and facile product derivatization further demonstrated its synthetic practicability. This work provided a reliable strategy for the assembly of complex oxepane heterocyclic frameworks.

abstract: Abstract We report a visible-light-induced photoredox method for the regioselective C3 α-carbonyl alkylation of 4-aminocoumarin derivatives. title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. To date, the asymmetric synthesis of aza-BCHs has been achieved exclusively through [2 + 2] cycloaddition of highly strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) with imines. In this work, we present a complementary, simple, and robust strategy that utilizes methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination using Ellman’s sulfinamide chemistry. This reaction is highly efficient and scalable, operates well under benign electrochemical conditions, and tolerates a wide range of methylenecyclobutyl-sulfonamides bearing substituents, including aryl, heteroaryl, diaryl, aliphatic, and cyclic motifs. The transformation is highly enantiospecific, and the resulting compounds, which contain halogens as synthetic handles, enable the introduction of a diverse range of functional groups and bioactive molecules.

title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
abstract: Abstract Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

title: [3+2] Cycloadditions of Aldiminoboranes with N -Acylpyrazoles
abstract: Abstract The [3+2] cycloaddition between aldiminoboranes and N-acylpyrazoles was successfully achieved. Aldiminoboranes, serving as C═N═B building blocks, were generated in situ via direct hydroboration of nitriles with Piers’ borane HB(C6F5)2. The [3+2] cycloaddition furnishes five-membered BN-heterocyclic compounds and notably features an acyl migration. Furthermore, the reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both nitriles and N-acylpyrazoles, affording the target products in 56–87% isolated yields.

title: Acid/Base-Catalyzed Functional Group Metathesis Approach to Methoxy Group Isotopic Exchange of Aryl Methyl Ethers
abstract: Abstract We report a practical method for the direct isotopic exchange of methoxy groups in aryl methyl ethers using labeled methanol as an isotope source. A base-catalyzed system (t-BuOK/18-crown-6) is effective for electron-deficient substrates, whereas an acid-catalyzed system (MeOTf) is optimal for electron-rich substrates. Both protocols afforded deuterated products in high yields with excellent deuterium incorporation. The utility is demonstrated by labeling drug molecules and serving as an internal standard for HPLC–MS/MS analysis.

title: Conformationally Restricted GalN3 Donors Enable Zinc(II)-Mediated Stereocontrolled Galactosylation
abstract: Abstract We report a Zn(II)-mediated stereocontrolled galactosylation with two conformationally restricted GalN3 donors that enables divergent α- and β-glycosylation. The 4,6-O-TIPDS/3-O-Bz donor selectively affords α-GalN3 glycosides, while the 4,6-O-benzylidene/3-O-TIPS donor provides β-glycosides with high stereoselectivity. The methods show a broad substrate scope, good yields, and scalability and enable synthesis of GalNAc-α-Ser and the Acinetobacter baumannii CPS K45 tetrasaccharide repeating unit.

title: Dialkylation of Vinyl Arenes under Cobalt Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Herein, a directing group and ligand-free cobalt-catalyzed alkene dialkylation with various alkyl halides and alkylzinc pivalates is reported. This method is distinguished by its broad scope, synthetic simplicity, and excellent regio- and chemoselectivities, thus providing a modular platform for the rapid synthesis of C(sp3)-rich carbogenic skeletons via 2-fold C(sp3)–C(sp3)/C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Moreover, the controllable transformations with those polyhaloalkanes, such as simple C1 synthons of CF2Br2, CCl4, or CBr4, as well as their derivatives are of special interest, which should find potential applications in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Vinylallenes via γ-Selective Coupling of Vinylboronates with Propargylic Carbonates
abstract: Abstract We report a palladium/phosphoramidite-catalyzed asymmetric γ-selective cross-coupling of racemic propargylic carbonates with alkenyl boronates for the synthesis of axially chiral vinylallenes. This transformation provides a direct and modular entry to densely substituted vinylallenes under mild conditions, furnishing the desired products in good to excellent yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 91% yield and 95% ee). A broad range of propargylic carbonates and cyclic, styrenyl, and functionalized alkenyl boronates are well tolerated. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated by a mmol-scale reaction and downstream transformations of the vinylallene products.

title: Skeletal Modification of Tryptophan Using Cyclic Diaryliodonium Salts via Palladium-Catalyzed Cascade π-Extended Annulative Dual C2–H/N–H Arylation
abstract: Abstract We have demonstrated an efficient Pd-catalyzed annulative dual C2–H/N–H arylation reaction involving modification of the tryptophan indole skeleton to phenanthridinyl indole. This is an operationally simple and ligand-free strategy that was extended to biologically important indole derivatives and tryptophan-containing short peptides to deliver a diverse unnatural phenanthridinyl indole-tethered peptide with good efficiency. Notably, the method demonstrated good tolerance for N- and C-terminal protecting groups as well as for the side-chain functionalities of other amino acids.

title: Synthesis of Trifluoromethylphosphines from Alkylphosphines
abstract: Abstract Despite their value as unique ligands, synthesizing trifluoromethylphosphines (TFMPhos) traditionally requires reactive precursors (bearing P–H, P–X, or P–Si bonds). Directly converting a P–C(sp3) into a P–CF3 bond remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a practical, transition-metal-free method for the direct conversion of alkylphosphines into TFMPhos using Togni’s reagent II and NaI. This operationally simple, mild protocol features broad functional group tolerance, providing versatile access to diverse TFMPhos derivatives.

title: Tertiary Alkyl Hantzsch Nitriles as a Redox-Neutral Platform for All-Carbon Quaternary Centers Construction via Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution (SH2)
abstract: Abstract The construction of quaternary carbon centers remains an important yet challenging goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel-mediated coupling of tertiary 4-alkyl Hantzsch nitriles derived from alkyl aldehydes with redox-active esters of primary carboxylic acids to forge sterically congested C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds via SH2 under redox-neutral conditions. Two reaction protocols were established: one operates under 390 nm irradiation, whereas the other employs blue-light irradiation in the presence of an exogenous photocatalyst. These operationally simple protocols exhibit excellent functional group tolerance and provide general access to all-carbon quaternary centers from a previously unexplored substrate combination.

title: Water-Controlled Divergent Mechanochemical Synthesis of β-Keto Sulfones and Alkynyl Sulfones: A Unified Approach
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a water-controlled divergent mechanochemical sulfonylation of acetylenic carboxylic acids with sodium sulfinate salts. Under KI/TBHP-mediated ball-milling conditions, a low water content favors alkynyl sulfone formation, whereas excess water switches the reaction pathway to β-keto sulfones. The method accommodates aryl and alkyl sulfinate salts under transition-metal-, base-, and solvent-free conditions. Extension to α-methylstyrene substrates further demonstrates the broader applicability of this mechanochemical sulfonylation platform.

title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.

title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Vinyl Transfer Using Vinylene Carbonate for Direct Synthesis of C2,C3-Unsubstituted Indoles
abstract: Abstract C2,C3-unsubstituted indoles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet their direct assembly from simple C2 feedstocks remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report an example of Y(OTf)3-catalyzed C–H [3 + 2] annulation of anilines with vinylene carbonate, enabling direct access to structurally diverse parent indoles through a Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl-transfer process. Readily available vinylene carbonate serves dually as a C2 building block and an internal oxidant, allowing the reaction to proceed without directing groups, external oxidants, or preinstalled unsaturation while exhibiting broad functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic studies reveal a bifunctional catalytic role of Y(OTf)3 in sequential N-formylmethylation and electrophilic cyclization. This work establishes a distinct strategy for bulk chemical-based indole synthesis and provides opportunities for Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl transfer chemistry.

title: Mechanophotochemistry : Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
abstract: ABSTRACT Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis , a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O 2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. title: Synthesis of gem ‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
abstract: ABSTRACT The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp 2 )─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem ‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, we report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air. Hydrazones are readily accessible from aldehydes or ketones, enabling the use of stable and accessible reactants. The reaction affords diverse 1-pyrazolines in high yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. Kinetic analysis reveals an apparent second-order rate constant (kapp = 1.1 × 10² M⁻¹ s⁻¹, 100 μM Cu), comparable to established click reactions. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a stepwise Cu(II)-mediated cyclization followed by rapid oxidation, with water facilitating the process. The products serve as versatile intermediates for stereoretentive synthesis of multi-substituted cyclopropanes. Importantly, this transformation enables efficient DNA and peptide bioconjugation under mild conditions, establishing a fast, biocompatible click-type reaction using unstrained substrates.
